note: Tables with two or more CREATE TABLE definitions that cannot describe one table — each demands a NOT NULL column the other has no place for. D1 holds one table per name and every definition is IF NOT EXISTS, so the first to run wins and the rest are no-ops; the code written against the loser cannot insert a row. Which shape is live is NOT provable from this repository: top-level sql/*.sql files are applied by hand (scripts/migrate-d1.mjs enumerates only sql/migrations/*.sql), so file order does not settle it. Each entry records what IS provable — chiefly whether the worker's own writers agree with each other — and names the PRAGMA that would settle the rest. The gate fails on NEW entries and on entries here that no longer collide, so this list cannot go stale. Resolving one means converging the definitions and deleting its line.
resolve_with: npx wrangler d1 execute studioos-db --remote --command="PRAGMA table_info('<table>')"

tables.capital_calls: WRITERS DISAGREE. routes/legalcap.ts inserts (deal_id, syndicate_id, amount_cents, currency, …) against its own ensureSchema at legalcap.ts:72; routes/funds.ts and routes/capital.ts read WHERE limited_partner_id = ?, which is the shape sql/consolidate_capital_rebuild.sql builds (uid, limited_partner_id, lp_investor_id, project_id, amount REAL NOT NULL, …). No single table satisfies both: the rebuild shape has no deal_id or amount_cents, and requires amount + uid that legalcap never binds. At least one of the two capital-call paths is dead in production.
tables.metrics_snapshots: FIVE LIVE DEFINITIONS AND THEY DISAGREE, measured after sql/historical/ stopped being harvested: migrations/034_unmounted_routes.sql:54 (project_id, snapshot_date, mrr, active_users, notes, source); schema_baseline.sql:2994 (deal_id, snapshot_date, key_metrics, traction_score, ai_review, created_by plus ten named metric columns) — the production shape; routes/pipeline.ts:54, which creates that same shape at runtime and is why it is the one that exists; integrations/providers/stripe.ts:320 and routes/progress.ts:1657, both of which create or ensure the project_id/mrr shape. PRODUCTION IS THE deal_id SHAPE PLUS TEN ALTERED COLUMNS. progress.ts's ensureMetricsSnapshotsSchema takes the else branch on an existing table and ALTERs in arr/cac/ltv/monthly_churn_pct/new_users/net_burn/cash_balance/headcount/nrr_pct/paying_accounts — which is exactly the comma-after-created_by trail visible in the baseline. Its required list does NOT include project_id, mrr, active_users, notes or source, so those five were never added. CONSEQUENCE, MEASURED AGAINST THE BASELINE: progress.ts:1784 (the founder metrics-snapshot POST) names all five of them and stripe.ts:337 (the Stripe MRR sync) names four, so both throw 'no such column: project_id'. check-sqlite-columns cannot see it because each writer's own CREATE vouches for its names — the general union problem that guard's docblock says it does not fix and names THIS file as the complement for. Tracked as its own task; resolving it is a decision about whether a per-project metric time series is a separate table or five more ALTERs, not a rename. Task #183 fixed the other half: queueWorker.ts's three jobs no longer name the generic (scope, scope_id, metric_name, value) shape at all.
tables.ic_meetings: routes/calendar.ts inserts (uid, title, agenda, start_at, duration_min, deal_id, organizer_user_id, location_kind, location_uri) — the sql/calendar.sql:19 shape, which requires start_at and organizer_user_id. sql/schema_baseline.sql:1010 and migration 034 declare a variant requiring starts_at instead. The worker's reads (ORDER BY start_at, SELECT organizer_user_id) agree with the writer, so calendar.sql's shape is the one the code assumes throughout.
tables.founder_checkins: routes/calendar.ts inserts (uid, founder_user_id, counterpart_user_id, project_id, title, notes, start_at, duration_min, location_kind, location_uri) — the sql/calendar.sql:58 shape. sql/schema_baseline.sql:1017 and migration 034 declare a variant requiring user_id, which no writer binds. As with ic_meetings the worker is internally consistent; only the schema files disagree.
tables.wellbeing_resources: FOUR definitions, two shapes. Both INSERTs in routes/wellbeing.ts name (uid, category, name, description, url, region, is_24_7, is_free, sort_order[, created_by_user_id]) — the sql/financials_wellbeing.sql:48 and migration 052 shape, matching routes/wellbeing.ts:104's own ensureSchema. sql/schema_baseline.sql:1038 and migration 034 declare a variant requiring title, which nothing writes. The writer side is consistent; the two schema files are the outliers.
